successCriteria: I group the notes of each beat so the beat is easy to see.
I know /4 times use the 6/8 pattern with values doubled and /16 times with values halved.
I can spot and correct bars that hide the beat.

explanation.text: The rule of grouping is the same in every time signature: show each beat clearly. In compound time, group notes and rests exactly as you did in 6/8, 9/8 and 12/8. The pattern does not change; the note values do. In the /4 times every value is doubled, and in the /16 times every value is halved.

explanation.text: Notes of a beat that can be beamed are beamed together, one beam for each beat, never across a beat. Notes longer than a quaver cannot be beamed, so in the /4 times the three crotchets of a beat stand apart. Two-quaver beats follow the 2/4 pattern: 4/8 is grouped just as 2/4 is, and the difference is only that its beat is a quaver, so it has four beats, not two.
Show every beat. In /4 times double the values of 6/8; in /16 times halve them. 4/8 is grouped like 2/4.

steps: Six semiquavers fill the bar: 6 ÷ 3 = two beats.
Each beat is three semiquavers, beamed together.

provenance.authoredBy: Music Theory Path curriculum team (Brief 05, drafted with AI assistance; pending qualified teacher review)
provenance.notes: Original wording. Follows Grade 4 outcome 1 (grouping) and First Steps Grade 4 section 3 (pp. 81-82: 'the grouping is the same as in 6/8, 9/8 and 12/8 except that in /4 the values are doubled and in /16 halved'; 4/8 is grouped as 2/4). 2/8 follows the same one-beat-one-group idea; the book states the grouping for 4/8 only, so 2/8 is a TEACHER TO CONFIRM item. Rests are not asked in this lesson (partly silent beats and double-dotted rests have no verified convention, see the teacher pack). Every wrong bar still adds up: it breaks one grouping rule only.
